artefacts.content_markdown:
# Business Requirements Document

**Project:** An app where people can book home cleaners for one-off or re
**Domain:** booking_platform
**Generated:** 2026-09-24

## 1. Document Control
- **Status:** Draft — generated by AI Business Analyst Agent
- **Version:** 1.0
- **Prepared for:** Downstream Product, UX, and Design AI agents

## 2. Executive Summary
**Product:** An app where people can book home cleaners for one-off or recurring visits

**Target users:** auto answer for users

**Business opportunity / problem:** auto answer for users currently lack a dedicated, reliable way to complete the booking workflow this product addresses.

**Proposed solution:** A booking platform that lets customers discover, commit to, and track a service end-to-end, replacing manual coordination with a structured digital workflow.

**Expected business value:** Faster, more reliable bookings increase conversion and repeat usage while reducing the manual operational burden of running the business.

**High-level capabilities:**
- Authentication & Account Management
- User Profile Management
- Search & Discovery
- Service Catalog
- Booking & Checkout
- Scheduling & Availability
- Payments & Billing
- Provider Management
- Reviews & Ratings
- Notifications
- Customer Support & Help
- Admin & Operations Console
- Reporting & Analytics
- Security & Access Control
- Onboarding & Activation
- Privacy, Consent & Data Retention

## 3. Business Background
**Current business context:** Today, the booking workflow described in the business idea is handled manually or through disconnected, general-purpose tools.

**Existing process:** Customer -> Contact Provider manually -> Discuss details -> Check availability -> Confirm informally -> Arrange payment -> Booking happens

**Market / business situation:** The booking platform space rewards platforms that reduce friction and build trust between customer and provider.

**Why the product is needed:** Without a dedicated product, auto answer for users face avoidable friction, and the business cannot scale beyond what manual coordination allows.

**Current limitations:** No structured record of transactions, no built-in trust mechanisms, and no operational visibility into what is happening across the business.

**Business opportunity:** A purpose-built platform can capture the booking platform workflow digitally, creating a defensible, scalable business.

## 4. Problem Statement
| Problem Area | Current Pain Point | Business Impact |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery | auto answer for users have no dedicated, reliable way to find the right service today. | Lost time, inconsistent outcomes, and missed opportunities on both sides of the transaction. |
| Coordination | Arranging a booking currently relies on manual, ad-hoc communication. | Slower turnaround, higher error rate, and a poor experience that erodes trust. |
| Trust & Transparency | There is no consistent way to verify quality or track status once a commitment is made. | Users hesitate to commit, depressing conversion and repeat usage. |
| Payments | Payment handling today is manual or fragmented across tools. | Delayed payment, reconciliation errors, and disputes that consume operational time. |

## 5. Product Vision
**Product vision:** Become the default way auto answer for users handle the booking workflow described in the business idea.

**Desired future state:** Customers and Providers transact through a single trusted platform with full visibility into status at every step.

**Long-term business direction:** Expand from the core MVP workflow into the future enhancements identified in this document as usage and data mature.

**Core value proposition:** Faster, more trustworthy bookings than the manual alternative, with less operational overhead for the business running the platform.

## 6. Business Objectives
- Validate the core booking workflow with early auto answer for users
- Reduce the manual operational work required to run the business
- Increase transparency for customers and providers throughout a booking
- Reach initial operational and financial viability for the MVP scope

## 7. Goals, KPIs & Success Criteria
| KPI | Definition | Target | Measurement Method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conversion rate | Share of customers who complete a booking after starting one | TBD | Completed / started transactions |
| Completion rate | Share of confirmed bookings that reach a completed state | TBD | Completed / confirmed bookings |
| Customer satisfaction | Post-transaction satisfaction score | TBD | Average review rating / survey score |
| Retention | Share of customers who return for a second booking within 90 days | TBD | Repeat-user cohort analysis |
| Revenue | Total platform revenue from completed transactions | TBD | Sum of captured payments, net of refunds |
| Processing time | Time from booking creation to confirmation | TBD | Timestamp delta, averaged |
| Error rate | Share of transactions that fail or error before completion | TBD | Failed / attempted transactions |
| Support resolution time | Time from ticket creation to resolution | TBD | Timestamp delta, averaged per ticket |
| Provider utilization | Share of available provider capacity actually booked | TBD | Booked / available provider slots |

## 8. Scope

### 8.1 In Scope
- Core booking platform workflow: Authentication & Account Management, User Profile Management, Search & Discovery, Service Catalog, Booking & Checkout, Scheduling & Availability
- Basic user onboarding and account management

### 8.2 Out of Scope
- Advanced analytics/reporting beyond the core report groups (future phase)
- Multi-region/multi-currency support (future phase)

### 8.3 Non-Goals
- Building a general-purpose platform beyond the described domain
- Replacing every internal operational tool on day one

## 9. Stakeholders
| Stakeholder | Responsibility / Interest | Decision Authority |
|---|---|---|
| Business Sponsor / Product Owner | Accountable for the product's business outcomes and ROI | Final sign-off on scope and priorities |
| Product Management | Owns the product requirements and roadmap | Decides feature scope and priority within budget |
| Design / UX | Owns the user experience translating requirements into screens and flows | Approves UX approach; escalates conflicts with requirements |
| Engineering | Builds and maintains the system described in this document | Approves technical feasibility and estimates |
| Operations | Runs the platform day to day once live | Input on admin/operations tooling requirements |
| Finance | Cares about revenue, payment reconciliation, and payout accuracy | Approves payment and reporting requirements |
| Customer Support | Handles user-facing issues after launch | Input on support tooling and escalation paths |
| Security / Compliance | Ensures the product meets security and data-protection expectations | Can block launch on unresolved security findings |
| QA | Validates the product meets its documented requirements | Sign-off on test coverage before release |
| End Users (Customers/Providers) | Use the product to accomplish their goal | Indirect — feedback informs prioritization |

## 10. User Roles & Permissions
#### Customer
- **Purpose:** The demand-side user who searches for and completes Bookings.
- **Responsibilities:** Search, evaluate, and commit to Services; manage their own account and Booking history.
- **Main capabilities:** Search/browse, create Bookings, manage own profile, submit reviews, raise support tickets.
- **Permissions:** Full access to own data only
- **Restricted actions:** Cannot view or edit other users' data; cannot access Admin tooling.

#### Provider
- **Purpose:** The supply-side user who publishes Services and fulfils Bookings.
- **Responsibilities:** Maintain Service listings, manage availability, fulfil Bookings.
- **Main capabilities:** Create/edit own Services, manage own availability, view own Bookings and payouts.
- **Permissions:** Full access to own listings and transactions only
- **Restricted actions:** Cannot view other Providers' data; cannot moderate Services or access Admin tooling.

#### Support Agent
- **Purpose:** Resolves user-reported issues and tickets.
- **Responsibilities:** Respond to and resolve support tickets; escalate where necessary.
- **Main capabilities:** View relevant Booking/account context for a ticket; respond to and close tickets.
- **Permissions:** Read access to user/Booking data relevant to open tickets
- **Restricted actions:** Cannot perform destructive admin overrides without escalation.

#### Admin
- **Purpose:** Operates and moderates the platform.
- **Responsibilities:** Manage users, Services, and Bookings; moderate content; resolve disputes/exceptions.
- **Main capabilities:** Full read access; manual overrides with recorded reason; access to reporting and audit logs.
- **Permissions:** Broadest access in the system
- **Restricted actions:** All actions are logged; destructive actions require explicit confirmation.


| Role | Core Permissions |
|---|---|
| Customer | Full access to own data only |
| Provider | Full access to own listings and transactions only |
| Support Agent | Read access to user/Booking data relevant to open tickets |
| Admin | Broadest access in the system |

## 11. User Personas
#### Primary Customer
- **Role:** auto answer for users
- **Occupation:** Represents the platform's core demand-side user
- **Goals:** Find and complete a Booking for the right Service with minimal friction
- **Needs:** A fast, trustworthy way to find, evaluate, and commit to the right option
- **Pain points:** Today this requires manual effort, scattered information, or an unreliable ad-hoc process
- **Behaviors:** Compares a small number of options before committing; abandons if the process feels slow or untrustworthy
- **Expectations:** Clear pricing, fast confirmation, and visibility into status after committing

#### Active Provider
- **Role:** Provider offering Services on the platform
- **Occupation:** Represents the platform's core supply-side user
- **Goals:** Get discovered, win Bookings, and get paid reliably
- **Needs:** Simple listing management, predictable payouts, and manageable operational overhead
- **Pain points:** Manual coordination today is time-consuming and makes it hard to grow volume
- **Behaviors:** Actively manages availability/listings; monitors ratings and Booking requests closely
- **Expectations:** Low-friction onboarding, fair visibility, and timely payment

#### Operations / Admin User
- **Role:** Internal team member responsible for day-to-day platform operation
- **Occupation:** Operations or platform support staff
- **Goals:** Keep the platform running smoothly and resolve exceptions quickly
- **Needs:** A single place to see and act on flagged items, disputes, and support tickets
- **Pain points:** Without dedicated tooling, exception-handling relies on ad-hoc manual work
- **Behaviors:** Monitors dashboards and exception queues; intervenes when automated flows break down
- **Expectations:** Accurate, real-time visibility and clear audit trails for every action taken


## 12. Current-State Process
Today, a booking is arranged manually: the customer contacts a provider directly, they discuss details informally, check availability back and forth, confirm verbally or in writing, and arrange payment separately from the booking itself. There is no shared source of truth for either party.

**Current flow:** Customer -> Contact Provider manually -> Discuss details -> Check availability -> Confirm informally -> Arrange payment -> Booking happens

## 13. Future-State Process
The proposed platform replaces ad-hoc coordination with a structured flow: the customer browses or searches, selects a service and the relevant details, reviews the total cost, pays, and receives confirmation — with the provider notified and assigned automatically. Alternative and failure paths (payment failure, unavailable slot, cancellation) are handled explicitly rather than left to manual follow-up.

**Future flow:** Customer -> Browse/Search -> Select Service -> Select details -> Review -> Pay -> Confirmation -> Provider assignment -> Booking -> Review

## 14. User Journeys
**Customer Journey:** Customer discovers the platform, searches for a service, reviews options, completes a booking, and leaves a review after completion.

**Provider Journey:** Provider applies to join, is verified, publishes services, manages incoming bookings, and gets paid.

**Admin/Operations Journey:** Admin monitors the exception queue, moderates flagged services, resolves disputes, and reviews operational reports.

**Support Journey:** Support agent receives a ticket, reviews the linked account/transaction context, resolves or escalates, and closes with a resolution note.

## 15. Product Overview & Modules
| Module ID | Module | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| MOD-01 | Authentication & Account Management | Provides secure account creation, login, and session management so that Customers and Providers can access role-appropriate functionality. This module is the entry point that gates every authenticated action elsewhere in the product. |
| MOD-02 | User Profile Management | Lets Customers and Providers maintain the personal and account information the product needs to operate correctly — contact details, preferences, and (where relevant) payment or payout details. |
| MOD-03 | Search & Discovery | Helps a Customer find the right Service quickly through search, filtering, and browsing, translating an open-ended need into a short, relevant list of Services to choose from. |
| MOD-04 | Service Catalog | Maintains the authoritative set of Services a Provider offers, including descriptions, pricing, media, and availability status, so Customers always see accurate, up-to-date listings. |
| MOD-05 | Booking & Checkout | Lets a Customer commit to a Service — selecting details, reviewing cost, and confirming — and turns that intent into a tracked Booking record that both sides can rely on. |
| MOD-06 | Scheduling & Availability | Manages when a Service can actually be delivered — Provider availability windows, slot capacity, and conflict prevention — so a Customer only ever sees and books slots that are genuinely open. |
| MOD-07 | Payments & Billing | Handles the movement of money for every Booking — capturing payment, tracking its status, issuing refunds, and keeping a reliable financial record for reconciliation. |
| MOD-08 | Provider Management | Covers how a Provider joins the platform, gets verified, and manages their standing — the supply side of the marketplace that makes Services available to Customers in the first place. |
| MOD-09 | Reviews & Ratings | Captures Customer feedback after a Booking completes, giving future Customers a trust signal and giving Providers (and Admins) a feedback loop on quality. |
| MOD-10 | Notifications | Keeps every party informed of state changes that matter to them — Booking updates, account events, and operational alerts — through the right channel at the right time. |
| MOD-11 | Customer Support & Help | Gives a Customer or Provider a way to get help and gives Support staff the tools to resolve issues — from self-service help content to a tracked ticket when something needs a human. |
| MOD-12 | Admin & Operations Console | Gives internal Operations and Admin users the tools to run the platform day to day — managing users, Services, and Bookings, and stepping in when something needs manual attention. |
| MOD-13 | Reporting & Analytics | Turns raw product activity into the numbers the business needs to run itself — Booking volume and revenue for Finance, activity and quality metrics for Operations, and usage trends for Product. |
| MOD-14 | Security & Access Control | Ensures that every action in the product is performed by an authorized party and that sensitive data is protected — the cross-cutting layer every other module depends on. |
| MOD-15 | Onboarding & Activation | Guides a newly-registered Customer or Provider from account creation to their first successful core action, so the value of the product is obvious quickly instead of requiring them to figure it out unassisted. |
| MOD-16 | Privacy, Consent & Data Retention | Gives users control over their own data — requesting a copy of it, deleting their account, and managing consent for optional data uses — and ensures the platform actually enforces its stated retention policy rather than only describing one. |

## 17. Detailed Module Requirements
#### Authentication & Account Management
- **Purpose:** Provides secure account creation, login, and session management so that Customers and Providers can access role-appropriate functionality. This module is the entry point that gates every authenticated action elsewhere in the product.
- **Actors:** Customer, Provider, Admin
- **Inputs:** Email or phone identifier, Password or one-time code, Account profile details
- **Processing:** Validate the identifier format and check for an existing account -> Create the account record and assign a default role -> Issue an authenticated session on successful login -> Handle password reset and account recovery requests
- **Outputs:** Authenticated session, Account confirmation, Password reset confirmation
- **Business rules:** A Customer or Provider must verify their identifier (email or phone) before completing a Booking.; Accounts are uniquely identified by email or phone; duplicate accounts for the same identifier are not permitted.; After 5 consecutive failed login attempts, the account is temporarily locked for a cooldown period.
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Priority:** P0

#### User Profile Management
- **Purpose:** Lets Customers and Providers maintain the personal and account information the product needs to operate correctly — contact details, preferences, and (where relevant) payment or payout details.
- **Actors:** Customer, Provider
- **Inputs:** Name, contact details, Profile photo (optional), Preferences, Addresses
- **Processing:** Validate and persist profile edits -> Enforce which fields are editable per role -> Propagate profile changes to dependent records (e.g. display name on past Bookings)
- **Outputs:** Updated profile record, Confirmation of saved changes
- **Business rules:** A Customer or Provider may only view and edit their own profile, except where an Admin role is explicitly granted override access.; Changing the primary contact identifier (email/phone) requires re-verification.; A user's display name must be unique enough to avoid confusion in shared views (e.g. booking history, reviews) but is not required to be globally unique.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P0

#### Search & Discovery
- **Purpose:** Helps a Customer find the right Service quickly through search, filtering, and browsing, translating an open-ended need into a short, relevant list of Services to choose from.
- **Actors:** Customer
- **Inputs:** Search query, Filters (category, price, location, availability), Sort preference
- **Processing:** Parse and normalize the search query -> Apply active filters against the Service Catalog -> Rank and return matching results -> Track search-to-result and search-to-Booking conversion for analytics
- **Outputs:** Ranked list of matching Services, Zero-result guidance when nothing matches
- **Business rules:** Only active, published Services are returned in search and browse results.; Filters must be combinable (e.g. category AND price range AND location) rather than mutually exclusive.; Search relevance ranking must not be purchasable/manipulable by a Provider outside of clearly labeled promoted placements, if any exist.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P0

#### Service Catalog
- **Purpose:** Maintains the authoritative set of Services a Provider offers, including descriptions, pricing, media, and availability status, so Customers always see accurate, up-to-date listings.
- **Actors:** Provider, Admin, Customer
- **Inputs:** Service title, description, price, Category/tags, Media (photos), Availability/stock status
- **Processing:** Validate required fields before publishing -> Apply category and pricing rules -> Version/track edits to published Services -> Reflect availability/stock changes in near real time
- **Outputs:** Published Service listing, Draft saved confirmation, Out-of-stock/unavailable status
- **Business rules:** A Service must have a title, description, price, and at least one category before it can be published.; A Provider may only edit or remove their own Services; Admins may moderate any listing.; An Service that is out of stock or unavailable must not be bookable/purchasable until restocked or re-enabled.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P0

#### Booking & Checkout
- **Purpose:** Lets a Customer commit to a Service — selecting details, reviewing cost, and confirming — and turns that intent into a tracked Booking record that both sides can rely on.
- **Actors:** Customer, Provider, Admin
- **Inputs:** Selected Service, Quantity/date/time as applicable, Delivery/service address, Payment method
- **Processing:** Validate Service availability at the moment of Booking -> Calculate total cost including any fees or taxes -> Create the Booking record in a pending state -> Confirm the Booking once payment succeeds -> Notify both Customer and Provider of the confirmed Booking
- **Outputs:** Booking confirmation, Unique Booking ID, Updated Booking status
- **Business rules:** A Booking may only be created against an Service that is currently published and available.; The total cost shown to the Customer before confirmation must match the amount actually charged.; A Booking moves through a defined status lifecycle (pending, confirmed, in progress, completed, cancelled) and may not skip states.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P0

#### Scheduling & Availability
- **Purpose:** Manages when a Service can actually be delivered — Provider availability windows, slot capacity, and conflict prevention — so a Customer only ever sees and books slots that are genuinely open.
- **Actors:** Provider, Customer, Admin
- **Inputs:** Provider working hours/availability windows, Existing bookings, Buffer/lead-time rules
- **Processing:** Compute open slots from Provider availability minus existing bookings -> Apply buffer/lead-time rules -> Lock a slot briefly during Customer checkout to prevent double-booking -> Release the lock if checkout is abandoned
- **Outputs:** List of open slots, Confirmed slot assignment
- **Business rules:** A Provider may not have two confirmed Bookings that overlap in time.; A slot is held for the Customer for a limited window during checkout; if payment is not completed in that window, the slot is released.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P0

#### Payments & Billing
- **Purpose:** Handles the movement of money for every Booking — capturing payment, tracking its status, issuing refunds, and keeping a reliable financial record for reconciliation.
- **Actors:** Customer, Provider, Admin
- **Inputs:** Payment method details, Booking amount, Refund requests
- **Processing:** Tokenize and validate the payment method via the payment processor -> Capture (or authorize then capture) payment for the Booking amount -> Record the resulting payment status and processor reference -> Process refunds against the original payment method where applicable -> Reconcile processor records against internal Booking records
- **Outputs:** Payment confirmation, Payment status, Refund confirmation, Transaction record for reconciliation
- **Business rules:** Raw payment card details must never be stored directly by the platform; only a processor-issued token/reference is retained.; A refund may not exceed the original captured amount for that Booking.; A Booking is not considered confirmed until payment capture succeeds.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P0

#### Provider Management
- **Purpose:** Covers how a Provider joins the platform, gets verified, and manages their standing — the supply side of the marketplace that makes Services available to Customers in the first place.
- **Actors:** Provider, Admin
- **Inputs:** Provider application details, Verification documents (if applicable), Performance history
- **Processing:** Collect Provider application/onboarding details -> Run verification checks per the active vetting policy -> Approve, reject, or request more information -> Monitor ongoing Provider performance (ratings, cancellation rate, response time)
- **Outputs:** Provider approval/rejection decision, Provider status (active, suspended, under review)
- **Business rules:** Only an approved, active Provider may publish Services or accept Bookings.; A Provider whose rating or cancellation rate falls below the platform's minimum threshold is flagged for review.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P0

#### Reviews & Ratings
- **Purpose:** Captures Customer feedback after a Booking completes, giving future Customers a trust signal and giving Providers (and Admins) a feedback loop on quality.
- **Actors:** Customer, Provider, Admin
- **Inputs:** Star rating, Written review text, Booking reference
- **Processing:** Prompt the Customer to review after Booking completion -> Validate the review is tied to a genuine completed Booking -> Publish the review to the Service/Provider page -> Allow moderation of flagged reviews
- **Outputs:** Published review, Updated average rating for the Service/Provider
- **Business rules:** A Customer may only review a Booking they actually completed, and only once per Booking.; A Provider may publicly respond to a review but may not delete a review outright; disputed reviews go through Admin moderation.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P1

#### Notifications
- **Purpose:** Keeps every party informed of state changes that matter to them — Booking updates, account events, and operational alerts — through the right channel at the right time.
- **Actors:** Customer, Provider, Admin
- **Inputs:** Triggering system event, User notification preferences
- **Processing:** Match the triggering event to its notification template -> Resolve the recipient(s) and their preferred channel(s) -> Render and send the notification -> Record delivery status for support/debugging
- **Outputs:** Sent notification (email/SMS/push/in-app), Delivery status
- **Business rules:** A user may opt out of non-essential notification categories, but not out of security- and Booking-critical notifications (e.g. payment confirmation).; Notifications must be sent within a short, bounded delay of the triggering event to remain useful.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P0

#### Customer Support & Help
- **Purpose:** Gives a Customer or Provider a way to get help and gives Support staff the tools to resolve issues — from self-service help content to a tracked ticket when something needs a human.
- **Actors:** Customer, Provider, Support agent, Admin
- **Inputs:** Help request/ticket details, Booking reference (if related), Support agent responses
- **Processing:** Offer self-service help content matched to common questions -> Capture a support ticket when self-service isn't enough -> Route the ticket to a support agent -> Track ticket status through to resolution
- **Outputs:** Ticket confirmation, Ticket resolution, Help content
- **Business rules:** Every support ticket must be linked to the requesting user's account and, where relevant, the associated Booking.; A ticket may not be closed without a recorded resolution note.; A ticket that references a Booking must be visible to the agent alongside that Booking's current status and history.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P1

#### Admin & Operations Console
- **Purpose:** Gives internal Operations and Admin users the tools to run the platform day to day — managing users, Services, and Bookings, and stepping in when something needs manual attention.
- **Actors:** Admin, Operations
- **Inputs:** Search/filter criteria across users, Services, Bookings, Manual override actions
- **Processing:** Provide searchable views of core entities -> Support manual status overrides with a recorded reason -> Surface flagged/exception items needing attention -> Log every admin action for audit purposes
- **Outputs:** Updated entity state, Audit log entry
- **Business rules:** Every manual override performed by Admin/Operations must be recorded with the acting user, timestamp, and reason.; Destructive actions (e.g. removing a Provider, cancelling a Booking) require explicit confirmation before executing.; Admin/Operations views must never expose raw payment credentials, even to resolve a support case.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P0

#### Reporting & Analytics
- **Purpose:** Turns raw product activity into the numbers the business needs to run itself — Booking volume and revenue for Finance, activity and quality metrics for Operations, and usage trends for Product.
- **Actors:** Admin, Operations, Business sponsor
- **Inputs:** Underlying Booking, payment, user, and Service data
- **Processing:** Aggregate underlying event and entity data on a scheduled or on-demand basis -> Compute the defined KPIs and report views -> Present reports with filtering by date range and (where relevant) Provider/category
- **Outputs:** Report views/dashboards, Exportable data (e.g. CSV) where required
- **Business rules:** Financial reports must reconcile to the underlying payment records — no report may show a different total than the sum of its source transactions.; A report or export must only include data the requesting role is authorized to see (e.g. Support sees ticket data, not full financial detail).
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P1

#### Security & Access Control
- **Purpose:** Ensures that every action in the product is performed by an authorized party and that sensitive data is protected — the cross-cutting layer every other module depends on.
- **Actors:** All roles
- **Inputs:** Authenticated session/role, Requested action/resource
- **Processing:** Check the acting user's role against the permission required for the requested action -> Deny and log unauthorized attempts -> Encrypt sensitive data in transit and at rest -> Rate-limit sensitive endpoints (login, payment) to reduce abuse
- **Outputs:** Allow/deny decision, Security audit log entry
- **Business rules:** Every state-changing action must check the acting user's role/permission before executing, not only hide the option in the UI.; Sensitive data (payment details, identity documents) must be encrypted at rest and only decrypted for authorized processing.; A security audit log entry must never itself contain the raw sensitive data (e.g. full card numbers, passwords) involved in the event it records.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P0

#### Onboarding & Activation
- **Purpose:** Guides a newly-registered Customer or Provider from account creation to their first successful core action, so the value of the product is obvious quickly instead of requiring them to figure it out unassisted.
- **Actors:** Customer, Provider
- **Inputs:** Newly created account, Role selected at signup
- **Processing:** Determine the correct onboarding path for the account's role -> Track completion of each onboarding step -> Surface the next best action until the first core action is completed
- **Outputs:** Onboarding progress state, Completed/activated account
- **Business rules:** Onboarding must be skippable/dismissible and must never block access to the core product.; An account's onboarding state must persist across sessions and devices.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P1

#### Privacy, Consent & Data Retention
- **Purpose:** Gives users control over their own data — requesting a copy of it, deleting their account, and managing consent for optional data uses — and ensures the platform actually enforces its stated retention policy rather than only describing one.
- **Actors:** Customer, Provider, Admin
- **Inputs:** Account deletion request, Data export/access request, Consent choices
- **Processing:** Authenticate the requesting user before acting on a deletion or export request -> Delete or irreversibly anonymize personal data not otherwise required to be retained, within the published retention window -> Package a machine-readable export of the user's own data on request -> Record and honor granular consent choices for optional (non-essential) data uses
- **Outputs:** Deletion confirmation, Data export file, Updated consent record
- **Business rules:** A user-initiated account deletion request must be honored within the platform's published retention/deletion window; data required for legal/financial record-keeping may be retained only as long as that obligation requires, clearly separate from the rest of the deleted account.; A user may withdraw consent for any optional (non-essential) data use at any time, without needing to delete their entire account.; Withdrawing optional consent or requesting deletion must never be harder to do than the original opt-in/signup action.
- **Dependencies:** Authentication
- **Priority:** P1

## 23. Payment Requirements
- **Methods:** TBD — specific payment methods to be confirmed; commonly cards and/or digital wallets
- **Flow:** Customer confirms booking -> payment captured -> booking confirmed -> funds reconciled
- **Statuses:** Pending, Captured, Failed, Refunded, Partially Refunded
- **Failure retry:** Buyer may retry with the same or a different method without duplicating the transaction
- **Duplicate prevention:** A single confirmation action results in at most one successful charge
- **Refunds:** Full or partial refunds follow the active cancellation policy and are recorded against the original payment
- **Reconciliation:** Internal transaction records must reconcile against processor records on a regular schedule

- **Audit:** Append-only audit log of every administrative action

## 26. Security Requirements
- Every state-changing action must check the acting user's role/permission before executing, not only hide the option in the UI.
- Sensitive data (payment details, identity documents) must be encrypted at rest and only decrypted for authorized processing.
- A security audit log entry must never itself contain the raw sensitive data (e.g. full card numbers, passwords) involved in the event it records.
- All state-changing actions require server-side permission checks, independent of client UI.

**Threats & controls:**

| Threat | Example Control |
|---|---|
| Credential stuffing / brute-force login | Rate limiting and account lockout after repeated failures |
| Payment fraud | Tokenized payment handling via a PCI-compliant processor; anomaly monitoring |
| Data exposure via broken access control | Server-side role-based access control on every endpoint |
| Fake/duplicate accounts | Identifier verification and duplicate-account detection at registration |

## 27. Privacy & Compliance
Applicable privacy and regulatory requirements must be confirmed for the launch geography. In the interim, personal data should be minimized, encrypted at rest, and access-logged, with deletion honored on request.

## 28. Accessibility Requirements
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA across primary user flows unless the business context specifies another standard.
- All interactive elements must be reachable and operable via keyboard.
- Form fields must have accessible labels and clear, non-color-only error indication.

## 33. Risks & Mitigation
| Risk | Impact | Consequence | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low initial adoption if onboarding friction is too high | High | Slower-than-planned growth and delayed ROI | Streamline onboarding; measure and iterate on drop-off points |
| Payment processor outage or integration failure | High | Transactions cannot complete; direct revenue impact | Select a processor with strong uptime SLAs; design graceful failure/retry handling |
| Supply-demand imbalance (not enough sellers, or not enough buyers) | Medium | Poor marketplace liquidity undermines the core value proposition | Sequence go-to-market to seed supply before scaling demand marketing, or vice versa |
| Data breach exposing personal or payment information | High | Regulatory exposure, reputational damage, user trust loss | Encrypt sensitive data, minimize retention, follow the security requirements in this document |
| Regulatory/compliance requirements not yet confirmed for launch geography | Medium | Potential rework or launch delay if requirements surface late | Confirm applicable regulations early with legal/compliance review |
| Fraudulent transactions or fake accounts | Medium | Financial loss and erosion of trust between parties | Identity verification, rate limiting, anomaly monitoring on transactions |
| Key third-party dependency (payments, notifications, maps) changes pricing or terms | Medium | Unexpected cost or forced re-integration | Abstract third-party integrations behind an internal interface where practical |
| Scope creep beyond MVP during build | Medium | Delayed launch, diluted focus | Enforce the MVP prioritization (P0/P1) in this document as the build contract |

## 36. Acceptance Criteria
**Customer/Provider Registration**
- Given customer submits the form with all required fields valid, when they confirm, then a new record is created and is immediately visible to customer.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when customer attempts to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider, then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given customer lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider, then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what customer is authorized to see.

**View & Edit Profile**
- Given customer has unsaved changes, when they attempt to navigate away, then the system warns them before the changes are discarded.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when customer attempts to view and edit their own profile fields (name, contact details, preferences), with changes validated and saved immediately, then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given customer lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to view and edit their own profile fields (name, contact details, preferences), with changes validated and saved immediately, then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what customer is authorized to see.

**Keyword Search**
- Given no records match the current query or filters, when results are returned, then the system shows an explicit empty state rather than a blank screen.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when customer attempts to search the Service Catalog by free-text keyword, matching against Service titles and descriptions, and return ranked results, then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given customer lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to search the Service Catalog by free-text keyword, matching against Service titles and descriptions, and return ranked results, then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what customer is authorized to see.

**Create Service Listing**
- Given provider submits the form with all required fields valid, when they confirm, then a new record is created and is immediately visible to provider.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when provider attempts to create a new Service listing with title, description, price, category, and media, saving it as a draft until required fields are complete, then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given provider lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to create a new Service listing with title, description, price, category, and media, saving it as a draft until required fields are complete, then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what provider is authorized to see.

**Create Booking**
- Given customer submits the form with all required fields valid, when they confirm, then a new record is created and is immediately visible to customer.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when customer attempts to initiate a Booking for a selected Service, capturing all details required (date/time, quantity, address, etc, then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given customer lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to initiate a Booking for a selected Service, capturing all details required (date/time, quantity, address, etc, then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what customer is authorized to see.

**Set Availability**
- Given provider meets the preconditions, when they define recurring or one-off availability windows, which determine which slots are offered to Customers with valid input, then the system completes the action and confirms it clearly.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when provider attempts to define recurring or one-off availability windows, which determine which slots are offered to Customers, then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.

## 38. Release Strategy
**Phase 0 — Discovery:** Finalize requirements, policies, and architecture decisions.  
*Exit criteria: BRD, PRD, and UX specification reviewed and approved by stakeholders.*

**Phase 1 — MVP:** Deliver the P0/P1 functionality needed for a usable booking platform product.  
*Exit criteria: All P0 requirements implemented and passing QA; core flow demonstrable end-to-end.*

**Phase 1.1 — Stabilization:** Bug fixes, usability refinements, accessibility and performance hardening.  
*Exit criteria: No open P0/P1 defects; NFR targets met or explicitly deferred with sign-off.*

**Phase 2 — Expansion:** P2/P3 functionality and the future enhancements listed in this document.  
*Exit criteria: Prioritized backlog re-evaluated against post-launch metrics.*


## 39. Future Enhancements
- AI-assisted recommendations/matching
- Dynamic pricing
- Loyalty/rewards program
- Predictive analytics for demand/supply balancing
- AI-assisted customer support (chatbot triage)
- Subscription tiers for providers

## 40. Glossary
| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Customer | The demand-side user who searches for and completes a booking. |
| Provider | The supply-side user or party who offers a service on the platform. |
| Service | The core offering being discovered and transacted on the platform. |
| Booking | A confirmed commitment between Customer and Provider for a given service. |
| MVP | Minimum Viable Product — the smallest release that delivers real value and validates the core hypothesis. |
| P0 / P1 / P2 / P3 | Priority tiers used throughout this document: P0 = critical/blocking, P1 = must-have for MVP, P2 = should-have, P3 = could-have/future. |
| RBAC | Role-Based Access Control — restricting system actions based on a user's assigned role. |
| SLA | Service-Level Agreement/Target — a measurable commitment such as response time or uptime. |
| TBD | To Be Determined — a value intentionally left open pending further input, rather than invented. |
| NFR | Non-Functional Requirement — a quality attribute (performance, security, etc.) rather than a feature. |
| Authentication & Account Management | Provides secure account creation, login, and session management so that Customers and Providers can access role-appropriate functionality. This module is the entry point that gates every authenticated action elsewhere in the product. |
| User Profile Management | Lets Customers and Providers maintain the personal and account information the product needs to operate correctly — contact details, preferences, and (where relevant) payment or payout details. |
| Search & Discovery | Helps a Customer find the right Service quickly through search, filtering, and browsing, translating an open-ended need into a short, relevant list of Services to choose from. |
| Service Catalog | Maintains the authoritative set of Services a Provider offers, including descriptions, pricing, media, and availability status, so Customers always see accurate, up-to-date listings. |
| Booking & Checkout | Lets a Customer commit to a Service — selecting details, reviewing cost, and confirming — and turns that intent into a tracked Booking record that both sides can rely on. |
| Scheduling & Availability | Manages when a Service can actually be delivered — Provider availability windows, slot capacity, and conflict prevention — so a Customer only ever sees and books slots that are genuinely open. |
| Payments & Billing | Handles the movement of money for every Booking — capturing payment, tracking its status, issuing refunds, and keeping a reliable financial record for reconciliation. |
| Provider Management | Covers how a Provider joins the platform, gets verified, and manages their standing — the supply side of the marketplace that makes Services available to Customers in the first place. |
| Reviews & Ratings | Captures Customer feedback after a Booking completes, giving future Customers a trust signal and giving Providers (and Admins) a feedback loop on quality. |
| Notifications | Keeps every party informed of state changes that matter to them — Booking updates, account events, and operational alerts — through the right channel at the right time. |
| Customer Support & Help | Gives a Customer or Provider a way to get help and gives Support staff the tools to resolve issues — from self-service help content to a tracked ticket when something needs a human. |
| Admin & Operations Console | Gives internal Operations and Admin users the tools to run the platform day to day — managing users, Services, and Bookings, and stepping in when something needs manual attention. |
| Reporting & Analytics | Turns raw product activity into the numbers the business needs to run itself — Booking volume and revenue for Finance, activity and quality metrics for Operations, and usage trends for Product. |
| Security & Access Control | Ensures that every action in the product is performed by an authorized party and that sensitive data is protected — the cross-cutting layer every other module depends on. |
| Onboarding & Activation | Guides a newly-registered Customer or Provider from account creation to their first successful core action, so the value of the product is obvious quickly instead of requiring them to figure it out unassisted. |
| Privacy, Consent & Data Retention | Gives users control over their own data — requesting a copy of it, deleting their account, and managing consent for optional data uses — and ensures the platform actually enforces its stated retention policy rather than only describing one. |

## 41. Open Questions
- None outstanding — all discovery questions were answered

This backlog decomposes every functional requirement in the Business Requirements Document (72 total) into actionable, independently testable user stories.

## 3. Story-Breakdown Methodology
Every functional requirement identified in the Business Requirements Document (FR-IDs) was converted into exactly one user story, grouped into epics that align 1:1 with the product modules defined there. No requirement was sampled, summarized, or dropped in this conversion — each story keeps a direct `related_fr_ids` reference back to its source requirement so the two documents stay traceable. Stories are not a restatement of the requirement; each adds actor-level detail (preconditions, trigger, main/alternative/exception flow, and Given/When/Then acceptance criteria) that the requirement itself does not specify.

## 4. Personas / Actors
- **Primary Customer** (auto answer for users): Find and complete a Booking for the right Service with minimal friction
- **Active Provider** (Provider offering Services on the platform): Get discovered, win Bookings, and get paid reliably
- **Operations / Admin User** (Internal team member responsible for day-to-day platform operation): Keep the platform running smoothly and resolve exceptions quickly

## 5. Epic Overview
- **EPIC-001: Authentication & Account Management** — Provides secure account creation, login, and session management so that Customers and Providers can access role-appropriate functionality. This module is the entry point that gates every authenticated action elsewhere in the product.
- **EPIC-002: User Profile Management** — Lets Customers and Providers maintain the personal and account information the product needs to operate correctly — contact details, preferences, and (where relevant) payment or payout details.
- **EPIC-003: Search & Discovery** — Helps a Customer find the right Service quickly through search, filtering, and browsing, translating an open-ended need into a short, relevant list of Services to choose from.
- **EPIC-004: Service Catalog** — Maintains the authoritative set of Services a Provider offers, including descriptions, pricing, media, and availability status, so Customers always see accurate, up-to-date listings.
- **EPIC-005: Booking & Checkout** — Lets a Customer commit to a Service — selecting details, reviewing cost, and confirming — and turns that intent into a tracked Booking record that both sides can rely on.
- **EPIC-006: Scheduling & Availability** — Manages when a Service can actually be delivered — Provider availability windows, slot capacity, and conflict prevention — so a Customer only ever sees and books slots that are genuinely open.
- **EPIC-007: Payments & Billing** — Handles the movement of money for every Booking — capturing payment, tracking its status, issuing refunds, and keeping a reliable financial record for reconciliation.
- **EPIC-008: Provider Management** — Covers how a Provider joins the platform, gets verified, and manages their standing — the supply side of the marketplace that makes Services available to Customers in the first place.
- **EPIC-009: Reviews & Ratings** — Captures Customer feedback after a Booking completes, giving future Customers a trust signal and giving Providers (and Admins) a feedback loop on quality.
- **EPIC-010: Notifications** — Keeps every party informed of state changes that matter to them — Booking updates, account events, and operational alerts — through the right channel at the right time.
- **EPIC-011: Customer Support & Help** — Gives a Customer or Provider a way to get help and gives Support staff the tools to resolve issues — from self-service help content to a tracked ticket when something needs a human.
- **EPIC-012: Admin & Operations Console** — Gives internal Operations and Admin users the tools to run the platform day to day — managing users, Services, and Bookings, and stepping in when something needs manual attention.
- **EPIC-013: Reporting & Analytics** — Turns raw product activity into the numbers the business needs to run itself — Booking volume and revenue for Finance, activity and quality metrics for Operations, and usage trends for Product.
- **EPIC-014: Security & Access Control** — Ensures that every action in the product is performed by an authorized party and that sensitive data is protected — the cross-cutting layer every other module depends on.
- **EPIC-015: Onboarding & Activation** — Guides a newly-registered Customer or Provider from account creation to their first successful core action, so the value of the product is obvious quickly instead of requiring them to figure it out unassisted.
- **EPIC-016: Privacy, Consent & Data Retention** — Gives users control over their own data — requesting a copy of it, deleting their account, and managing consent for optional data uses — and ensures the platform actually enforces its stated retention policy rather than only describing one.

### US-001 — Customer/Provider Registration
*Epic: EPIC-001  |  Role: Customer  |  Related requirement(s): FR-001*

**Story:** As a Customer, I want to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider, so that I can do so quickly, reliably, and with confidence the result is correct.
**Business value:** The system shall allow a new Customer or Provider to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider. Required fields, format validation, and duplicate-account prevention must be enforced before the account is created.
**Preconditions:** Customer does not already have an account
**Trigger:** Customer initiates the 'Customer/Provider Registration' action

**Main flow:**
  1. Customer opens the create/add action to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider
  2. Customer fills in the required fields
  3. System validates each required field as it is entered and again on submit
  4. System saves the new record (as Draft or Pending where the module defines that status)
  5. System confirms creation and displays the newly created record

**Alternative flow:** None
**Exception flow:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction

**Business rules:**
- A Customer or Provider must verify their identifier (email or phone) before completing a Booking.
- Accounts are uniquely identified by email or phone; duplicate accounts for the same identifier are not permitted.
- After 5 consecutive failed login attempts, the account is temporarily locked for a cooldown period.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Given customer submits the form with all required fields valid, when they confirm, then a new record is created and is immediately visible to customer.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when customer attempts to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider, then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given customer lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider, then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what customer is authorized to see.

### US-069 — Request Account Deletion
*Epic: EPIC-016  |  Role: Customer  |  Related requirement(s): FR-069*

**Story:** As a Customer, I want to request deletion of my account and associated personal data, confirm the request, and receive confirmation once it has been processed, so that I can do so quickly, reliably, and with confidence the result is correct.
**Business value:** The system shall allow a Customer or Provider to request deletion of their account and associated personal data, confirm the request, and receive confirmation once it has been processed.
**Preconditions:** Customer is authenticated and has the permissions required for this action
**Trigger:** Customer initiates the 'Request Account Deletion' action

**Main flow:**
  1. Customer navigates to the relevant screen
  2. Customer provides the information required to request deletion of their account and associated personal data, confirm the request, and receive confirmation once it has been processed
  3. System validates the input
  4. System completes the action and confirms the result

**Alternative flow:** None
**Exception flow:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction

**Business rules:**
- A user-initiated account deletion request must be honored within the platform's published retention/deletion window; data required for legal/financial record-keeping may be retained only as long as that obligation requires, clearly separate from the rest of the deleted account.
- A user may withdraw consent for any optional (non-essential) data use at any time, without needing to delete their entire account.
- Withdrawing optional consent or requesting deletion must never be harder to do than the original opt-in/signup action.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Given customer meets the preconditions, when they request deletion of their account and associated personal data, confirm the request, and receive confirmation once it has been processed with valid input, then the system completes the action and confirms it clearly.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when customer attempts to request deletion of their account and associated personal data, confirm the request, and receive confirmation once it has been processed, then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.

artefacts.content_markdown:
# Product Requirements Document (PRD)

**Project:** An app where people can book home cleaners for one-off or re
**Generated:** 2026-09-24

## 1. Product Overview
An app where people can book home cleaners for one-off or recurring visits. This product addresses the problems identified in the Business Requirements Document by giving auto answer for users a structured, end-to-end digital workflow in place of manual coordination.

## 2. Product Goals
- Validate the core booking workflow with early auto answer for users
- Reduce the manual operational work required to run the business
- Increase transparency for customers and providers throughout a booking
- Reach initial operational and financial viability for the MVP scope

## 3. Target Users & Personas
**Target users:** auto answer for users

- **Primary Customer** (auto answer for users) — Find and complete a Booking for the right Service with minimal friction
- **Active Provider** (Provider offering Services on the platform) — Get discovered, win Bookings, and get paid reliably
- **Operations / Admin User** (Internal team member responsible for day-to-day platform operation) — Keep the platform running smoothly and resolve exceptions quickly

## 4. User Journeys
- Customer Journey: Customer discovers the platform, searches for a service, reviews options, completes a booking, and leaves a review after completion.
- Provider Journey: Provider applies to join, is verified, publishes services, manages incoming bookings, and gets paid.
- Admin/Operations Journey: Admin monitors the exception queue, moderates flagged services, resolves disputes, and reviews operational reports.
- Support Journey: Support agent receives a ticket, reviews the linked account/transaction context, resolves or escalates, and closes with a resolution note.

## 5. Product Capabilities
- Authentication & Account Management
- User Profile Management
- Search & Discovery
- Service Catalog
- Booking & Checkout
- Scheduling & Availability
- Payments & Billing
- Provider Management
- Reviews & Ratings
- Notifications
- Customer Support & Help
- Admin & Operations Console
- Reporting & Analytics
- Security & Access Control
- Onboarding & Activation
- Privacy, Consent & Data Retention

## 6. Functional Requirements
### FR-001 — Customer/Provider Registration

The system shall allow a new Customer or Provider to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider. Required fields, format validation, and duplicate-account prevention must be enforced before the account is created.
- **Outputs:** Confirmation of the completed action, Updated record state
- **User-visible result:** User sees a clear success confirmation and, where applicable, the updated record

- **Validation:** Enforces: A user-initiated account deletion request must be honored within the platform's published retention/deletion window; data required for legal/financial record-keeping may be retained only as long as that obligation requires, clearly separate from the rest of the deleted account.; A user may withdraw consent for any optional (non-essential) data use at any time, without needing to delete their entire account.
- **Error scenarios:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction, Permission denied for the acting role, Required field missing or fails format validation
- **Dependencies:** FR-002

### FR-071 — Consent Management
- **Purpose:** The system shall let a user view and change their consent choices for optional (non-essential) data uses, separate from the notification-preferences settings.
- **Actor:** Customer
- **Trigger:** Customer initiates the 'Consent Management' action
- **Preconditions:** Customer is authenticated and has the permissions required for this action
- **Inputs:** Customer changes the relevant setting to make use of "Consent Management"
- **Expected behavior:** System performs: Consent Management. The system shall let a user view and change their consent choices for optional (non-essential) data uses, separate from the notification-preferences settings.
- **Outputs:** Confirmation of the completed action, Updated record state
- **User-visible result:** User sees a clear success confirmation and, where applicable, the updated record
- **Validation:** Enforces: A user-initiated account deletion request must be honored within the platform's published retention/deletion window; data required for legal/financial record-keeping may be retained only as long as that obligation requires, clearly separate from the rest of the deleted account.; A user may withdraw consent for any optional (non-essential) data use at any time, without needing to delete their entire account.
- **Error scenarios:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction, Permission denied for the acting role, Required field missing or fails format validation
- **Dependencies:** FR-002

### FR-072 — Data Retention Enforcement
- **Purpose:** The system shall automatically enforce the platform's data retention policy, removing or anonymizing personal data once its retention period has elapsed, independent of an explicit deletion request.
- **Actor:** Customer
- **Trigger:** Customer initiates the 'Data Retention Enforcement' action
- **Preconditions:** Customer is authenticated and has the permissions required for this action
- **Inputs:** Customer provides the information required to make use of "Data Retention Enforcement"
- **Expected behavior:** System performs: Data Retention Enforcement. The system shall automatically enforce the platform's data retention policy, removing or anonymizing personal data once its retention period has elapsed, independent of an explicit deletion request.
- **Outputs:** Confirmation of the completed action, Updated record state
- **User-visible result:** User sees a clear success confirmation and, where applicable, the updated record
- **Validation:** Enforces: A user-initiated account deletion request must be honored within the platform's published retention/deletion window; data required for legal/financial record-keeping may be retained only as long as that obligation requires, clearly separate from the rest of the deleted account.; A user may withdraw consent for any optional (non-essential) data use at any time, without needing to delete their entire account.
- **Error scenarios:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction, Permission denied for the acting role, Required field missing or fails format validation
- **Dependencies:** FR-002


## 7. Roles & Permissions
- **Customer:** Search/browse, create Bookings, manage own profile, submit reviews, raise support tickets.
- **Provider:** Create/edit own Services, manage own availability, view own Bookings and payouts.
- **Support Agent:** View relevant Booking/account context for a ticket; respond to and close tickets.
- **Admin:** Full read access; manual overrides with recorded reason; access to reporting and audit logs.

## 8. Product Business Rules
- BR-001: A Customer or Provider must verify their identifier (email or phone) before completing a Booking.
- BR-002: Accounts are uniquely identified by email or phone; duplicate accounts for the same identifier are not permitted.
- BR-003: After 5 consecutive failed login attempts, the account is temporarily locked for a cooldown period.
- BR-004: A Customer or Provider may only view and edit their own profile, except where an Admin role is explicitly granted override access.
- BR-005: Changing the primary contact identifier (email/phone) requires re-verification.
- BR-006: A user's display name must be unique enough to avoid confusion in shared views (e.g. booking history, reviews) but is not required to be globally unique.
- BR-007: Only active, published Services are returned in search and browse results.
- BR-008: Filters must be combinable (e.g. category AND price range AND location) rather than mutually exclusive.
- BR-009: Search relevance ranking must not be purchasable/manipulable by a Provider outside of clearly labeled promoted placements, if any exist.
- BR-010: A Service must have a title, description, price, and at least one category before it can be published.
- BR-011: A Provider may only edit or remove their own Services; Admins may moderate any listing.
- BR-012: An Service that is out of stock or unavailable must not be bookable/purchasable until restocked or re-enabled.
- BR-013: A Booking may only be created against an Service that is currently published and available.
- BR-014: The total cost shown to the Customer before confirmation must match the amount actually charged.
- BR-015: A Booking moves through a defined status lifecycle (pending, confirmed, in progress, completed, cancelled) and may not skip states.
- BR-016: A Provider may not have two confirmed Bookings that overlap in time.
- BR-017: A slot is held for the Customer for a limited window during checkout; if payment is not completed in that window, the slot is released.
- BR-018: Raw payment card details must never be stored directly by the platform; only a processor-issued token/reference is retained.
- BR-019: A refund may not exceed the original captured amount for that Booking.
- BR-020: A Booking is not considered confirmed until payment capture succeeds.
- BR-021: Only an approved, active Provider may publish Services or accept Bookings.
- BR-022: A Provider whose rating or cancellation rate falls below the platform's minimum threshold is flagged for review.
- BR-023: A Customer may only review a Booking they actually completed, and only once per Booking.
- BR-024: A Provider may publicly respond to a review but may not delete a review outright; disputed reviews go through Admin moderation.
- BR-025: A user may opt out of non-essential notification categories, but not out of security- and Booking-critical notifications (e.g. payment confirmation).
- BR-026: Notifications must be sent within a short, bounded delay of the triggering event to remain useful.
- BR-027: Every support ticket must be linked to the requesting user's account and, where relevant, the associated Booking.
- BR-028: A ticket may not be closed without a recorded resolution note.
- BR-029: A ticket that references a Booking must be visible to the agent alongside that Booking's current status and history.
- BR-030: Every manual override performed by Admin/Operations must be recorded with the acting user, timestamp, and reason.
- BR-031: Destructive actions (e.g. removing a Provider, cancelling a Booking) require explicit confirmation before executing.
- BR-032: Admin/Operations views must never expose raw payment credentials, even to resolve a support case.
- BR-033: Financial reports must reconcile to the underlying payment records — no report may show a different total than the sum of its source transactions.
- BR-034: A report or export must only include data the requesting role is authorized to see (e.g. Support sees ticket data, not full financial detail).
- BR-035: Every state-changing action must check the acting user's role/permission before executing, not only hide the option in the UI.
- BR-036: Sensitive data (payment details, identity documents) must be encrypted at rest and only decrypted for authorized processing.
- BR-037: A security audit log entry must never itself contain the raw sensitive data (e.g. full card numbers, passwords) involved in the event it records.
- BR-038: Onboarding must be skippable/dismissible and must never block access to the core product.
- BR-039: An account's onboarding state must persist across sessions and devices.
- BR-040: A user-initiated account deletion request must be honored within the platform's published retention/deletion window; data required for legal/financial record-keeping may be retained only as long as that obligation requires, clearly separate from the rest of the deleted account.
- BR-041: A user may withdraw consent for any optional (non-essential) data use at any time, without needing to delete their entire account.
- BR-042: Withdrawing optional consent or requesting deletion must never be harder to do than the original opt-in/signup action.

## 9. Navigation Behavior
Primary navigation surfaces the core booking platform workflow first (Authentication & Account Management, User Profile Management, Search & Discovery, Service Catalog); secondary items (settings, account, support) are accessible but not primary.

## 10. Notifications & Confirmations
- Account created — delivered via Email + In-app
- Email/phone verification — delivered via Email + In-app
- Password reset requested — delivered via Email + In-app
- Password changed — delivered via Email + In-app
- Suspicious login detected — delivered via Email + In-app
- Profile updated — delivered via In-app + Push
- Contact identifier changed — delivered via In-app + Push
- Listing published — delivered via In-app + Push
- Listing out of stock — delivered via In-app + Push
- Listing flagged/moderated — delivered via In-app + Push
- Booking created — delivered via In-app + Push
- Booking confirmed — delivered via In-app + Push

## 11. Validation & Error Handling
All forms validate required fields client-side before submission; server-side validation errors are surfaced with actionable, field-specific messages. Every functional requirement above defines its own error scenarios explicitly rather than relying on a single generic error state.

## 12. State Behaviors
- **Loading:** Show a loading indicator while an action is processing
- **Empty:** Show a clear empty state with a call to action when no data exists yet
- **Success:** Show explicit confirmation of the completed action
- **Failure:** Show a clear error message with a retry or correction path
- **Processing:** Disable the triggering action while in progress to prevent duplicate submissions

## 13. Audit & Versioning
Admin/Operations actions are recorded in an append-only audit log (see BRD Section 24). Full version history of records is not required for the MVP scope.

## 14. Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-001 [Performance] The system shall respond to standard user-facing actions within 2 seconds under normal load.
- NFR-002 [Performance] Search and listing pages shall return results within 1.5 seconds for catalogs up to 100,000 items.
- NFR-003 [Scalability] The system shall support horizontal scaling of stateless application components as transaction volume grows.
- NFR-004 [Scalability] The data layer shall support at least 10x current expected launch volume without architectural rework.
- NFR-005 [Availability] Core user-facing functionality shall target 99.5% monthly uptime post-launch.
- NFR-006 [Reliability] A failed payment or network error shall never leave a transaction in an ambiguous or double-charged state.
- NFR-007 [Security] All traffic between client and server shall be encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher.
- NFR-008 [Security] The system shall enforce role-based access control on every state-changing server endpoint.
- NFR-009 [Privacy] Personally identifiable information shall be encrypted at rest and access-logged.
- NFR-010 [Accessibility] All primary user flows shall meet WCAG 2.2 AA where applicable.
- NFR-011 [Usability] First-time users shall be able to complete the core workflow without external instructions.
- NFR-012 [Maintainability] The codebase shall follow a documented architecture and coding standard to support ongoing maintenance.
- NFR-013 [Compatibility] The system shall support the latest two major versions of common desktop and mobile browsers.
- NFR-014 [Monitoring] The system shall emit structured logs and metrics sufficient to diagnose production incidents.
- NFR-015 [Logging] Security-relevant events (login, permission denial, payment) shall be logged with actor, timestamp, and outcome.
- NFR-016 [Backup] Production data shall be backed up on a regular, automated schedule with tested restore procedures.
- NFR-017 [Disaster Recovery] A documented recovery plan shall define target recovery time and recovery point objectives.
- NFR-018 [Localization] Text content shall be externalized to support future localization, even if only one language ships at launch.

## 15. Technical & Integration Constraints
- **Application type:** Recommended: responsive web application; TBD: native mobile app for a later phase
- **Major system capabilities:** Authentication & Account Management; User Profile Management; Search & Discovery; Service Catalog; Booking & Checkout; Scheduling & Availability; Payments & Billing; Provider Management; Reviews & Ratings; Notifications; Customer Support & Help; Admin & Operations Console; Reporting & Analytics; Security & Access Control; Onboarding & Activation; Privacy, Consent & Data Retention
- **External integrations:** Payment Gateway; Email Delivery; SMS / OTP Provider; Maps / Geolocation; Analytics
- **Data sources:** Account records; Profile records; SearchQuery records; Service records; Booking records; AvailabilityWindow records
- **Api dependencies:** Payment Gateway API; Email Delivery API; SMS / OTP Provider API; Maps / Geolocation API
- **Real time requirements:** Slot-holding during checkout requires near-real-time availability checks; otherwise standard request/response is sufficient.
- **Authentication dependencies:** Recommended: managed authentication provider rather than custom-built auth
- **Platform deployment constraints:** POC/MVP scope — single environment and region initially, not yet designed for multi-region deployment
- **Per-capability technical notes:**
  - **Payments & Billing:** Payments & Billing: payment capture/refunds are delegated to a tokenizing, PCI-compliant processor; the platform never stores raw card data and only holds a processor-issued reference.
  - **Scheduling & Availability:** Scheduling & Availability: slot computation and a short-lived hold during checkout must be handled with a concurrency-safe check to prevent two confirmations of the same slot.

## 16. Security, Privacy & Access Constraints
- **Authentication requirements:** All core workflow actions require an authenticated session (see FR-001/FR-002 in the Functional Requirements above)
- **Mfa requirements:** Not required for MVP — Recommended for Admin roles in a later phase
- **Roles:** Customer; Provider; Support Agent; Admin
- **Access restrictions:** Customer: Cannot view or edit other users' data; cannot access Admin tooling.; Provider: Cannot view other Providers' data; cannot moderate Services or access Admin tooling.; Support Agent: Cannot perform destructive admin overrides without escalation.; Admin: All actions are logged; destructive actions require explicit confirmation.
- **Sensitive data handling:** Payment data must never be stored directly — delegated to a PCI-compliant processor (see BRD Section 23)
- **Privacy requirements:** Applicable privacy and regulatory requirements must be confirmed for the launch geography. In the interim, personal data should be minimized, encrypted at rest, and access-logged, with deletion honored on request.
- **Audit requirements:** Admin/Operations actions are logged; see BRD Section 24
- **Approval requirements:** None identified from discovery
- **Ux implications:** Admin-only actions (e.g. approve/reject, moderation, overrides) must not be shown to non-Admin roles; Payment entry screens must clearly indicate secure handling
- **Per-capability security notes:**
  - **Authentication & Account Management:** Authentication & Account Management: passwords/OTPs are hashed/never logged in plaintext; sessions expire on idle timeout and are invalidated on password change.
  - **User Profile Management:** User Profile Management: a user may only view/edit their own profile; changing the primary contact identifier requires re-verification.
  - **Payments & Billing:** Payments & Billing: raw payment credentials are never stored by the platform; only a processor token/reference is retained, and refunds cannot exceed the original captured amount.
  - **Admin & Operations Console:** Admin & Operations Console: every manual override is recorded with actor, timestamp, and reason in an append-only audit log; destructive actions require explicit confirmation.
  - **Privacy, Consent & Data Retention:** Privacy, Consent & Data Retention: account deletion and data-export requests are authenticated before acting on them; deleted data is removed or irreversibly anonymized within the published retention window.

## 17. AI Feature Specifications
*This product has no AI-powered features per the business idea and discovery answers.*

## 18. MVP / Phase 2 / Future Scope

### MVP Scope
- FR-001 — Customer/Provider Registration
- FR-002 — Login
- FR-006 — View & Edit Profile
- FR-011 — Keyword Search
- FR-012 — Filter Results
- FR-016 — Create Service Listing

- FR-019 — Manage Availability/Stock
- FR-021 — Create Booking
- FR-022 — Review Before Confirming
- FR-023 — Booking Confirmation
- FR-027 — Set Availability
- FR-028 — View Open Slots
- FR-029 — Prevent Double-Booking
- FR-031 — Capture Payment
- FR-033 — Prevent Duplicate Charges
- FR-036 — Provider Onboarding

- FR-044 — Event-Triggered Notifications
- FR-052 — Manage Users
- FR-061 — Role-Based Access Control
- FR-063 — Data Encryption

- FR-007 — Manage Addresses
- FR-018 — Publish / Unpublish Listing
- FR-024 — View Booking History
- FR-025 — Cancel Booking
- FR-032 — Retry Failed Payment
- FR-034 — Process Refunds
- FR-035 — Payment & Payout Records
- FR-039 — Suspend / Reinstate Provider
- FR-040 — Submit Review
- FR-041 — Display Reviews
- FR-047 — Submit Support Ticket
- FR-048 — Track Ticket Status
- FR-049 — Agent Ticket Queue
- FR-053 — Manage Services
- FR-054 — Manage Bookings
- FR-057 — Operational Dashboard
- FR-058 — Revenue & Booking Reports
- FR-062 — Rate Limiting
- FR-066 — Guided First-Run Walkthrough
- FR-069 — Request Account Deletion

### Phase 2 Scope
- FR-005 — Session & Logout
- FR-009 — Account Deactivation
- FR-013 — Sort Results
- FR-014 — Zero-Result Handling
- FR-020 — Category Browsing
- FR-026 — Modify Booking

- FR-067 — Onboarding Progress Checklist

### Future Scope
- FR-008 — Profile Photo
- FR-010 — Notification Preferences (Profile)
- FR-015 — Recent & Saved Searches
- FR-042 — Provider Response
- FR-045 — Notification Preferences
- FR-050 — Self-Service Help Content

### Out of Scope

- Multi-region/multi-currency support (future phase)

## 19. Success Metrics
- Conversion rate
- Completion rate
- Customer satisfaction
- Retention
- Revenue
- Processing time
- Error rate
- Support resolution time
