## 20. Dependencies

- Email Delivery

- Maps / Geolocation

## 21. Assumptions
- ASSUMPTION: auto answer for users have internet-connected devices.
- ASSUMPTION: Initial launch targets a single geography.
- ASSUMPTION: A payment processor will be available and integrated for MVP.

## 22. Release Plan

- **Phase 1 — MVP**: Deliver the P0/P1 functionality needed for a usable booking platform product.
- **Phase 1.1 — Stabilization**: Bug fixes, usability refinements, accessibility and performance hardening.

artefacts.title: UX Product Flow Specification — An app where people can book home cleaners for one-off or re
artefacts.content_markdown:
# UX / Product Flow Specification

**Project:** An app where people can book home cleaners for one-off or re
**Generated:** 2026-09-24

*This is the primary document intended for the external Design AI Agent.
It describes what each screen must contain and how it must behave — not
visual designs.*

## 1. Application Information Architecture
- Sign Up / Log In
- Dashboard / Home
- User Profile Management
- Search & Discovery
- Service Catalog
- Booking & Checkout
- Scheduling & Availability
- Payments & Billing
- Provider Management
- Reviews & Ratings
- Customer Support & Help
- Admin & Operations Console
- Reporting & Analytics
- Onboarding & Activation
- Privacy, Consent & Data Retention
- Account Settings

## 2. Screen Inventory
### SCR-001 — Sign Up / Log In
- **Purpose:** Authenticate the user or create a new account
- **Primary role:** Customer
- **Entry points:** First visit, Logged-out state
- **Exit points:** Dashboard
- **Related stories:** US-001, US-002
- **Related requirements:** FR-001, FR-002
- **Primary actions:** Sign up, Log in
- **Secondary actions:** Forgot password
- **Navigation:** Entry point before any authenticated screen
- **Information displayed:** Sign-up/login form
- **Data required:** Email/identifier, Password
- **UI elements required:** Text input, Password input, Submit button
- **Permissions:** Public — no authentication required
- **Business rules:** Requires a valid, unique identifier
- **Dependencies:** N/A

### SCR-002 — Dashboard / Home
- **Purpose:** Primary landing screen after authentication, orienting the user to their next action
- **Primary role:** Customer
- **Entry points:** Post sign-up/login
- **Exit points:** SCR-003, SCR-004, SCR-005
- **Related stories:** US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005
- **Related requirements:** FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, FR-004, FR-005
- **Primary actions:** Navigate to core workflow
- **Secondary actions:** Access settings
- **Navigation:** Reached immediately after authentication; primary hub for navigation
- **Information displayed:** Summary of recent/upcoming activity
- **Data required:** Customer's recent Bookings
- **UI elements required:** Navigation menu, Activity summary, Primary call-to-action
- **Permissions:** Authenticated Customer
- **Business rules:** N/A
- **Dependencies:** SCR-001

### SCR-003 — User Profile Management — Create / Edit
- **Purpose:** Create / Edit for User Profile Management: View & Edit Profile; Manage Addresses; Profile Photo
- **Primary role:** Customer
- **Entry points:** SCR-002
- **Exit points:** SCR-002
- **Related stories:** US-006, US-007, US-008
- **Related requirements:** FR-006, FR-007, FR-008
- **Primary actions:** View & Edit Profile, Manage Addresses, Profile Photo
- **Secondary actions:** Cancel, Go back
- **Navigation:** Reached from the Dashboard via User Profile Management navigation
- **Information displayed:** View & Edit Profile: The system shall allow an authenticated user to view and edit their own profile fields (name, contact details, preferences), with changes validated and saved immediately., Manage Addresses: The system shall allow a Customer to add, edit, and remove one or more saved addresses, and to designate a default address used to pre-fill future Bookings., Profile Photo: The system shall allow a user to upload, replace, or remove a profile photo, with size and format validation applied before storage.
- **Data required:** Profile — Profile ID, Account ID, Display name, Contact details, Address(es)
- **UI elements required:** Form fields, Save button, Cancel button, Inline validation messages
- **Permissions:** Authenticated Customer
- **Business rules:** A Customer or Provider may only view and edit their own profile, except where an Admin role is explicitly granted override access., Changing the primary contact identifier (email/phone) requires re-verification., A user's display name must be unique enough to avoid confusion in shared views (e.g. booking history, reviews) but is not required to be globally unique.
- **Dependencies:** SCR-002

### SCR-004 — User Profile Management — Settings
- **Purpose:** Settings for User Profile Management: Account Deactivation; Notification Preferences (Profile)
- **Primary role:** Customer
- **Entry points:** SCR-002
- **Exit points:** SCR-002
- **Related stories:** US-009, US-010
- **Related requirements:** FR-009, FR-010
- **Primary actions:** Account Deactivation, Notification Preferences (Profile)
- **Secondary actions:** Cancel, Go back
- **Navigation:** Reached from the Dashboard via User Profile Management navigation
- **Information displayed:** Account Deactivation: The system shall allow a user to request account deactivation, after which the account is disabled for login while historical Booking records are retained per the data retention policy., Notification Preferences (Profile): The system shall let a user manage basic profile-level preferences (language, contact preference) from within their profile, separate from per-category notification settings.
- **Data required:** Profile — Profile ID, Account ID, Display name, Contact details, Address(es)
- **UI elements required:** Form fields, Toggle controls, Save button
- **Permissions:** Authenticated Customer
- **Business rules:** A Customer or Provider may only view and edit their own profile, except where an Admin role is explicitly granted override access., Changing the primary contact identifier (email/phone) requires re-verification., A user's display name must be unique enough to avoid confusion in shared views (e.g. booking history, reviews) but is not required to be globally unique.
- **Dependencies:** SCR-002

### SCR-005 — Search & Discovery
- **Purpose:** Browse & Search for Search & Discovery: Keyword Search; Filter Results; Sort Results; Zero-Result Handling; Recent & Saved Searches
- **Primary role:** Customer
- **Entry points:** SCR-002
- **Exit points:** SCR-002
- **Related stories:** US-011, US-012, US-013, US-014, US-015
- **Related requirements:** FR-011, FR-012, FR-013, FR-014, FR-015
- **Primary actions:** Keyword Search, Filter Results, Sort Results, Zero-Result Handling, Recent & Saved Searches
- **Secondary actions:** Clear filters
- **Navigation:** Reached from the Dashboard via Search & Discovery navigation
- **Information displayed:** Keyword Search: The system shall allow a Customer to search the Service Catalog by free-text keyword, matching against Service titles and descriptions, and return ranked results., Filter Results: The system shall allow a Customer to narrow search or browse results using category, price range, and (where applicable) location and availability filters, with the result count updating as filters are applied., Sort Results: The system shall allow a Customer to sort results by relevance, price, rating, or newest, persisting the chosen sort within the session., Zero-Result Handling: The system shall present clear guidance (e.g. suggested filter changes) when a search or filter combination returns no results, rather than a blank screen.
- **Data required:** SearchQuery — Query ID, Search text, Filters applied, Result count, Timestamp
- **UI elements required:** Search input, Filter controls, Sort dropdown, Results list/grid, Empty state
- **Permissions:** Authenticated Customer
- **Business rules:** Only active, published Services are returned in search and browse results., Filters must be combinable (e.g. category AND price range AND location) rather than mutually exclusive., Search relevance ranking must not be purchasable/manipulable by a Provider outside of clearly labeled promoted placements, if any exist.
- **Dependencies:** SCR-002

### SCR-006 — Service Catalog — Browse & Search
- **Purpose:** Browse & Search for Service Catalog: Category Browsing
- **Primary role:** Provider
- **Entry points:** SCR-002
- **Exit points:** SCR-002
- **Related stories:** US-020
- **Related requirements:** FR-020
- **Primary actions:** Category Browsing
- **Secondary actions:** Clear filters
- **Navigation:** Reached from the Dashboard via Service Catalog navigation
- **Information displayed:** Category Browsing: The system shall organize Services into browsable categories so a Customer can explore the Service Catalog without an explicit search query.
- **Data required:** Service — Service ID, Provider ID, Title, Description, Price
- **UI elements required:** Search input, Filter controls, Sort dropdown, Results list/grid, Empty state
- **Permissions:** Authenticated Provider
- **Business rules:** A Service must have a title, description, price, and at least one category before it can be published., A Provider may only edit or remove their own Services; Admins may moderate any listing., An Service that is out of stock or unavailable must not be bookable/purchasable until restocked or re-enabled.
- **Dependencies:** SCR-002

### SCR-007 — Service Catalog — Create / Edit
- **Purpose:** Create / Edit for Service Catalog: Create Service Listing; Edit Service Listing; Publish / Unpublish Listing; Manage Availability/Stock
- **Primary role:** Provider
- **Entry points:** SCR-002
- **Exit points:** SCR-002
- **Related stories:** US-016, US-017, US-018, US-019
- **Related requirements:** FR-016, FR-017, FR-018, FR-019
- **Primary actions:** Create Service Listing, Edit Service Listing, Publish / Unpublish Listing, Manage Availability/Stock
- **Secondary actions:** Cancel, Go back
- **Navigation:** Reached from the Dashboard via Service Catalog navigation
- **Information displayed:** Create Service Listing: The system shall allow a Provider to create a new Service listing with title, description, price, category, and media, saving it as a draft until required fields are complete., Edit Service Listing: The system shall allow a Provider to edit an existing Service listing's details, with changes reflected to Customers immediately upon save., Publish / Unpublish Listing: The system shall allow a Provider to publish a completed listing (making it visible in search/browse) or unpublish it (hiding it without deleting the underlying record)., Manage Availability/Stock: The system shall allow a Provider to mark an Service as unavailable/out of stock, automatically preventing new Bookings against it until it is re-enabled.
- **Data required:** Service — Service ID, Provider ID, Title, Description, Price
- **UI elements required:** Form fields, Save button, Cancel button, Inline validation messages
- **Permissions:** Authenticated Provider
- **Business rules:** A Service must have a title, description, price, and at least one category before it can be published., A Provider may only edit or remove their own Services; Admins may moderate any listing., An Service that is out of stock or unavailable must not be bookable/purchasable until restocked or re-enabled.
- **Dependencies:** SCR-002

### SCR-008 — Booking & Checkout — Create / Edit
- **Purpose:** Create / Edit for Booking & Checkout: Create Booking; Booking Confirmation; Cancel Booking; Modify Booking
- **Primary role:** Customer
- **Entry points:** SCR-002
- **Exit points:** SCR-002
- **Related stories:** US-021, US-023, US-025, US-026
- **Related requirements:** FR-021, FR-023, FR-025, FR-026

## 3. User Flows
### FLOW-001 — Flow: Customer/Provider Registration
- **Actor:** Customer
- **Goal:** The system shall allow a new Customer or Provider to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider. Required fields, format validation, and duplicate-account prevention must be enforced before the account is created.
- **Starting point:** Dashboard
- **Preconditions:** Customer does not already have an account
- **Main path:**
    1. Customer opens the create/add action to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider (SCR-001)
    2. Customer fills in the required fields
    3. System validates each required field as it is entered and again on submit
    4. System saves the new record (as Draft or Pending where the module defines that status)
    5. System confirms creation and displays the newly created record
- **Alternative paths:** None
- **Error paths:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction
- **Decision points:** None
- **Completion state:** Action completed and confirmed to the user
- **Related screens:** SCR-002, SCR-001
- **Related requirements:** FR-001
- **Related stories:** US-001

### FLOW-002 — Flow: Login
- **Actor:** Customer
- **Goal:** The system shall allow a registered user to authenticate using their identifier and password (or one-time code), establishing a session that persists across page reloads until logout or expiry.
- **Starting point:** Dashboard
- **Preconditions:** Customer has a registered, verified account
- **Main path:**
    1. Customer opens the create/add action to authenticate using their identifier and password (or one-time code), establishing a session that persists across page reloads until logout or expiry (SCR-001)
    2. Customer fills in the required fields
    3. System validates each required field as it is entered and again on submit
    4. System saves the new record (as Draft or Pending where the module defines that status)
    5. System confirms creation and displays the newly created record
- **Alternative paths:** None
- **Error paths:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction

## 5. Interactions
- **Customer/Provider Registration** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for Customer/Provider Registration; behavior: The system shall allow a new Customer or Provider to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider. Required fields, format validation, and duplicate-account prevention must be enforced before the account is created.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error

## 7. Navigation
- **Primary:** Left sidebar (desktop) / bottom tab bar (mobile) exposing Dashboard plus one entry per core module
- **Secondary:** Account settings and support accessible from a persistent header menu
- **Mobile:** Bottom tab bar collapses secondary items into a 'More' menu

## 8. Notifications & Feedback
- **Success:** Toast/banner confirming the action, auto-dismissing after a few seconds
- **Error:** Inline field-level errors plus a summary banner for form-level failures
- **Loading:** Skeleton or spinner in place of content; primary actions disabled while in flight
- **Empty:** Illustration or message plus a clear primary call to action

## 9. Roles & Permissions Matrix
| Role | View | Edit | Approve | Reject |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customer | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Provider | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Support Agent | Yes | No | No | No |
| Admin | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

## 10. Responsive Requirements
- **Desktop:** Full multi-column layouts; primary navigation always visible
- **Tablet:** Collapsible navigation; core flows remain single-column where content is form-heavy
- **Mobile:** Single-column layouts; bottom tab navigation; touch targets at least 44x44px

## 11. Accessibility
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA across primary user flows unless the business context specifies another standard.
- All interactive elements must be reachable and operable via keyboard.
- Form fields must have accessible labels and clear, non-color-only error indication.
